A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChemMAS research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the revised pagination and numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original private-dataset comparisons, component and training ablations, agent-collaboration experiments, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds public-benchmark results, interpretability measurements, reward-component ablations, and dataset-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The General Chemist, retrieval, tournament selection, debate, Qwen3-8B backbone, and SFT/GRPO procedures remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(12), algorithms, and agent prompts retain their substantive procedures. Some accuracy/similarity wording changes do not establish a different training objective; the binary Acc reward remains specified.

E1.justification: V2 adds the ChemCoTBench-RCR test population: 90 examples covering ten reaction types, with separate catalyst, solvent, and reagent questions, presented as OOD evaluation. It also evaluates functional-group, by-product, reaction-type, and rationale outputs rather than assessing only recommended conditions. The original private dataset remains.

E2.justification: The private-data comparison retains RCR, Reagent Transformer, MM RCR, and the same five general-purpose LLMs. The new public-benchmark and interpretability comparisons reuse those five LLMs. No new external comparator or substitution is introduced.

E3.justification: V1 reports Top-k accuracy; v2 specifies maximum-over-top-k composite fingerprint Tanimoto similarity, including invalid-SMILES handling and exclusion of stereochemistry. V2 also introduces expert-reference accuracies, BLEU-4, and question-based LLM judging. The original split and shared candidate-ranking protocol remain; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds OOD generalization testing, mechanistic-output and rationale-quality diagnostics, and separate ablations of Acc and the multi-tool bonus rM in Table 4. Figure 6 adds molecular-distribution analyses across dataset splits. Earlier component, training-stage, and agent-combination ablations and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new evaluations retain point-score reporting; dataset histograms do not introduce uncertainty estimates for performance.

E6.justification: New results include ChemCoTBench Top-1 similarities of 62.1/57.8/51.2 for catalyst/solvent/reagent, mechanistic-output accuracies of 95.8/90.2/92.5, and ChemMAS LLM-Score 92.8 with BLEU-4 0.26. Reward-ablation results are also added. Original private-data and retained ablation values are numerically unchanged despite their metric relabeling, so they show no demonstrated cross-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix E introduces formal definitions of the validity-weighted Fingerprint Tanimoto Score and composite Score@k, particularly Equations (19)–(20). These change the mathematical specification of evaluation. The original framework and training mathematics remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion redefine headline performance gains from Top-1 accuracy to Top-1 structural similarity while retaining the numerical gain claims. This materially changes what the central empirical superiority claim means. The proposed evidence-based reasoning contribution itself remains.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets public-benchmark performance as reasoning beyond near-duplicate retrieval and interpretability scores as evidence of scientifically sound explanations. It also attributes benefits specifically to correctness and multi-tool reward terms. These extend the existing mechanistic and generalization narrative without substantially revising its limitations.

D1.justification: New Appendices E/F document RDKit requirements, canonicalization, fingerprint parameters, invalid-input treatment, private-data provenance and preprocessing, and public-benchmark composition. This substantially expands reproducibility information. The previously reported backbone, optimization settings, training budget, and eight-A100 hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Li et al. (2025), the ChemCoTBench reference, and Yang et al. (2026), LungNoduleAgent. The related-work organization and positioning around missing why-level explanations otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose is retained. V2 adds dedicated generalization and interpretability subsections, condenses the conclusion, updates terminology and the conference header, and reorganizes the appendices. The former prompt and supplementary-results sections move to G/H following new evaluation and dataset sections.

P2.justification: V2 adds a public-benchmark table, a multipart interpretability figure, and six dataset-distribution plots. It expands the training-ablation table, adds improvement annotations to the main comparison, and uses a denser conference layout. Original schematics, prompts, collaboration plots, and qualitative examples remain, with renumbering and caption changes.

improvement.justification: Explicit scoring and dataset documentation, a public benchmark, interpretability checks, and targeted reward ablations improve transparency and evidential support beyond v1. The gains are limited by unreconciled accuracy-to-similarity relabeling of identical values, remaining accuracy labels in figures, and missing sample-size, annotation-procedure, and judge-model details for the interpretability evaluation.
